title: story-003's slippage floor is denominated over the combined total, whose larger half is minted unconditionally, so every minPhUSDOut in [0, amount] - including the figure a caller naturally computes - is provably unable to fire, and the caller's stablecoin half settles at whatever rate is live with no revert and no on-chain trace that a floor was ever stated

faithfulnessNote: Deliberately NOT tagged faithfulness and NOT routed to spec-conformance as a deviation. The implementation is FAITHFUL to story-003: the story's own Technical Details prescribe `if (mintedForStable + amount < minPhUSDOut) revert InsufficientPhUSDOut(...)` verbatim, and the executor's only departure was hoisting the sum into a local (Autonomous Decision 3), which is behaviour-identical. This is therefore the Law-1-overrides-Law-2 case: the story's OWN intended behaviour is the defect. The unsafe-story flag that Law 1 mandates is filed as F-05 (a507f00ae1fbc38c) and routed to spec-conformance; the CODE-level impact is carried here at its honest band, so nothing is double-counted.
incompleteFixOf: 3aac91383dcb6060 (F-01, fix-pending, human-set - status NOT changed by this stage)
c4Criterion: Medium (2) - 'leak value with a hypothetical attack path with stated assumptions, but external requirements'. The value leak is real, demonstrated and irreversible; it is gated on an external requirement (a live exchange rate below parity) that no attacker can create, that the caller does not control, and that arises from an ordinary, sanctioned owner operation rather than from an attack.

classification.assetImpact: USER assets, not protocol assets. A caller who annihilates while the registered exchange rate R is below parity surrenders `amount` (18-dec) of a real stablecoin, pulled at :246 and deposited irreversibly into the yield strategy through PhusdStableMinter.mint, and receives amount + amount*R/1e18 phUSD instead of 2*amount. The stablecoin cannot be recovered: PhusdStableMinter exposes no redeem, burn or withdraw entry point (verified by grep at 3a96fb7, zero hits), and Antimatter holds no residue (StableNotDeposited at :255 asserts the balance returned to its pre-call value). BINDING (ADJ-02): the protocol balance sheet strictly IMPROVES at every R < 1e18. This must never be written up as a protocol value leak.
attackPath: 0. PRECONDITION (external, not attacker-created): the owner has set the registered exchangeRate for `stable` below 1e18. PhusdStableMinter.updateExchangeRate is onlyOwner (PhusdStableMinter.sol:138) and exists precisely so the owner can re-price a depegged stable - it is an ordinary operational act.

1. Alice holds 100e18 antimatter and 100e6 USDC. She reads the NatSpec at :222-225, which tells her minPhUSDOut is 'the least phUSD the caller will accept in total, counting both halves' and that passing zero waives the protection.

2. She reasons in the natural units of the trade: the antimatter half is fixed at `amount`, so the only leg that can move is the stable half. She sets minPhUSDOut = 100e18 - i.e. 'at worst give me back what my antimatter alone is worth'. This is a NON-ZERO floor and she believes she is protected.
3. annihilate burns her 100e18 antimatter at :239 (irreversible, effects-first) and pulls her 100e6 USDC at :246.
4. At R = 6e17 the minter mints 60e18 phUSD for the stable half. :259 computes totalPhUSD = 100e18 + 60e18 = 160e18.
5. :260 evaluates `160e18 < 100e18` -> false. The floor does not fire. The call SETTLES.

6. Alice receives 160e18 phUSD against the 200e18 the documented 2x property promises - a 40e18 (20% of total, 40% of the stable leg) shortfall - and the Annihilated event at :266 emits totalPhUSD as if normal, with minPhUSDOut appearing nowhere in the event, so no on-chain record exists that a floor was ever stated.

7. At the R = 0 endpoint the same path delivers only the antimatter half and the entire stablecoin is consumed for nothing (that endpoint is carried separately by ledger 0ed1c6e3270816c5 / L-03, whose mitigation is orthogonal).

GENERALISATION (proven, not extrapolated): step 5 holds for EVERY minPhUSDOut in [0, amount] and every R. Halmos check_invA_d18 and check_invA_d06 both PASS over an unbounded domain (amount, minPhUSDOut, R all full uint256), so `totalPhUSD < minPhUSDOut` is unsatisfiable throughout that band. The useful range of the guard begins one wei above `amount`.
classification.likelihood: MODERATE, and higher than the fix record implies. It needs no attacker, no race and no unusual caller behaviour - only (a) R below parity at execution time and (b) a caller who states a floor at or below the antimatter half. (b) is the natural choice, not a mistake: the antimatter half is the only figure the caller knows exactly, `amount` is the only quantity in the signature to anchor on, and the NatSpec presents ZERO as THE opt-out without ever saying that [1, amount] waives identically. The project's own suite reinforces the error - all six floor tests use values strictly above `amount`, so no test in the repository demonstrates the inert band. (a) is the ordinary operating state the owner was told was safe: F-01's human triageReason sanctioned deleting the protocol-side zero guard on the premise that 'a post-burn revert unwinds the whole transaction anyway', a premise Halmos INV-A now refutes over exactly this band.
assumptions: The registered exchangeRate R for the chosen stable is below 1e18 at the moment the transaction lands. At R == 1e18 (parity) there is no shortfall at all and this finding has no impact.
The caller states a floor in [0, amount] rather than strictly above `amount`.

The caller values the stablecoin they surrender at more than R per unit - i.e. the rate is stale, mis-set, or set to zero. Where R correctly reflects a genuine depeg the nominal shortfall is a correct re-pricing and the caller's ECONOMIC loss is smaller than the 40% nominal figure. The severity is carried on the mis-set / stale / zero cases, and this qualification must survive into the write-up.
classification.externalRequirements: An owner rate movement below parity, via PhusdStableMinter.updateExchangeRate (onlyOwner, in a nested read-only dependency). No attacker can create this condition and no attacker profits from it: the surrendered stablecoin goes to the yield strategy, not to a counterparty. There is no theft, no sandwich and no permissionless trigger.

law3.test: Would a competent, non-malicious owner be surprised by this consequence? YES.
law3.reasoning: The owner shipped a parameter named minPhUSDOut, documented as caller protection, whose entire lower half is inert. Nothing in the source, the NatSpec, the tests or the story's acceptance record says so. This is a non-obvious footgun surfaced as an operational hazard at honest severity - it is NOT a malicious-owner vector and must never be written up as one.
safeConfigGuidance: Until the guard is re-denominated, treat any exchangeRate below 1e18 as a state in which annihilate is unsafe for callers, and pause the stable (setStablecoinEnabled false) rather than re-pricing it downward, so annihilate reverts inside minter.mint before settling.

Any UI or integrator must compute minPhUSDOut as `amount + expectedStableLeg` with real slippage tolerance, and must never submit a value <= amount - a value in that band is silently equivalent to submitting zero.

justification: MEDIUM, and the High/Medium line is where this finding actually turns, so the reasoning is recorded rather than asserted. The case FOR High is not weak: real user assets are irreversibly lost, the mechanism carries no hypotheticals whatsoever (Halmos proves the guard unsatisfiable over [0, amount] on an unbounded domain, with four required-fail falsifiability controls confirming the harness observes reverts rather than pruning them), and C4's High limb reads 'stolen/LOST/compromised' - loss without theft can be High. Three things hold it at Medium, and they are properties of the C4 text, not of a wish to keep the report tidy. FIRST, there is no attack path in the C4 sense, because there is no attacker: no party gains the caller's stablecoin, no party can create the triggering condition, and no permissionless action moves the protocol into the loss state. The loss is a MISSING PROTECTION that fails to defend against an ordinary configuration, which is precisely the shape C4 places at Medium and precisely why its Medium limb is worded as 'leak value ... with stated assumptions, but external requirements' rather than as an attack. SECOND, the external requirement is load-bearing and is not satisfied at HEAD by default: at parity the shortfall is exactly zero, so the loss is gated on an owner action in a nested dependency that the caller neither triggers nor observes. Reporting the 40% figure as an unconditional outcome would overstate it. THIRD, part of the nominal shortfall is not economic loss at all - where R tracks a genuine depeg, paying 160 phUSD for 100 antimatter plus 100 units of a $0.60 stablecoin is correct pricing, and the honest residual is confined to stale, mis-set and zero rates. Set against that, this must NOT be understated either, and three specific temptations are refused: it is not dismissible as a caller footgun (the caller who states the natural non-zero floor is exercising the protection, not declining it), it is not dismissible under the yield-funded-pot opportunity-cost carve-out (a real stablecoin leaves the caller's balance and cannot be recovered), and it is not dismissible on the story's own acceptance record (that record's stated ground - 'standard minOut == 0 DeFi behaviour, a protection the caller opted out of' - is refuted by the proof, since [1, amount] waives exactly as completely as 0). Medium is the honest band: the protocol's function is impaired in the specific sense that the only protection annihilate offers its callers does not work over the half of its domain callers will naturally use.

recommendation.primary: Denominate the floor on the leg that can actually move. Either check the stable leg alone (`if (mintedForStable < minPhUSDOut) revert ...`, re-documenting minPhUSDOut as a stable-leg minimum), or keep the combined total and reject a floor that cannot bind (`if (minPhUSDOut != 0 && minPhUSDOut <= amount) revert FloorCannotBind(minPhUSDOut, amount);`), so a caller who states a floor in the inert band is told rather than silently unprotected.
recommendation.secondary: Emit minPhUSDOut in the Annihilated event so a settled annihilation carries an on-chain record of the protection the caller asked for.
recommendation.documentation: The NatSpec at :222-225 presents 0 as THE opt-out. It must state that every value <= amount waives identically. This is the documentationGap carried forward from the sanitizer and it travels with this finding, not with Q-05.
recommendation.orthogonalAndNotASubstitute: Restoring a protocol-side, non-waivable `if (mintedForStable == 0) revert PhUSDNotReceived();` after :256 closes ledger 0ed1c6e3270816c5's R == 0 endpoint but does NOT close this finding (it is silent for every R in (0, 1e18)). Conversely this finding's fix does not close 0ed1c6e3270816c5 for a caller who genuinely passes zero. Both are owed.
